form: A neat little two-storey brick cottage at the edge of the wood, a small copy of the family's north-Oxford villa redrawn in the dream's Art Nouveau: steep slate roof, one broad gable chimney stack, brass-plated front door on the lane side, a kitchen-garden yard with a cucumber-frame under the upstairs window at the back

grows_from.waking_detail: the family's own house and housemaid; the dream shrinks the villa Alice sees from the bank into a servant-sized house where she is taken for the maid

mucha_design_language.item: Mucha / Art Nouveau on a neat villa-cottage: window heads and door head in flowing horseshoe curves of pale yellow brick with carved stone lily-and-vine hood moulds; a round stained-glass halo roundel in the gable plaque (pastel roses and gold); a narrow mosaic frieze of pastel-and-gold vine tesserae under the eaves; the brass door plate framed by a whiplash border; wrought-iron whiplash gutter brackets and a gilded iron finial on the gable; the paling fence of the yard with flowing tops. Clean and well kept (Mary Ann's house), unlike the Duchess's sooted house
mucha_design_language.culture_ref: world.json#WR-010 (the White Rabbit's house listed); cultivation.json#XA-magic-08
mucha_design_language.why: Replaces the Gothic Revival trim; the brick and slate of the waking villa stay so the grows_from link reads

structure.item: footprint about 6.0 m wide x 5.0 m deep, two storeys, eaves at 5.2 m, ridge at 8.0 m
structure.why: 'a neat little house'; small enough to fill with a grown Alice, tall enough for ladders tied together

structure.item: front (north, lane side): central front door with a bright brass plate engraved W. RABBIT, one ground-floor sash window each side
back (south, yard side): one upstairs sash window of the upstairs room, directly above a glazed cucumber-frame
structure.note: window on a different side from the door: the Rabbit must 'go round' to reach it (ch004-p14)

structure.item: east gable end: one broad brick chimney stack rising 1.5 m above the ridge with two clay pots; the flue at the top about 45 x 45 cm
structure.note: flue size inferred so Bill (photoreal CGI lizard) is lowered and kicked out through it; size kept for the layout

structure.item: south-east corner of the yard: firm level ground where the ladders are put up and tied together
yard: a small kitchen garden with a dug patch under an old apple tree (Pat 'digging for apples'), a low paling fence, the wood behind

materials.item: red brick with bands and horseshoe-curved window heads of pale yellow brick
materials.why: The waking villa's polychrome brick ties the dream house to the waking house; the arch line is the dream's Art Nouveau

materials.item: blue-grey Welsh slate roof with a few loose and slipped slates near the chimney

materials.why: Period standard, and pebbles can rattle in at an opened sash

materials.item: front door painted dark bottle green, four-panel, with a polished brass plate, brass knocker and brass knob
cucumber-frame: low wooden box frame with sloping glass lights

details.item: carved stone hood moulds of flowing lily-and-vine relief over the windows and a round stained-glass halo roundel in the gable plaque
details.why: Same Art Nouveau vocabulary as the dream's hall

details.item: a broken glass light in the cucumber-frame after the Rabbit's fall
a boot scraper and a swept stone step at the front door
details.why: Marks a house a housemaid keeps (Mary Ann)

scale_notes.anchor: The house stays human-scale, the scale of the dream household Alice is taken into (Pat is a human performer; the White Rabbit, Bill and the crowd of little animals are photoreal CGI animals per SUP-002 as amended BIB-0027, at sizes set by 04-creatures); Alice arrives at a size that lets her be taken for the housemaid.

builds.beat: arrival, the siege, ladders, Bill down the chimney and kicked out, pebbles thrown, Alice runs out
builds.build: 1:1 full exterior with a working roof section and chimney stack rig

builds.beat: Alice's giant arm out of the upstairs window, snatching at the Rabbit; the whole window filled by an arm
builds.build: 1:3 miniature south wall and window (window about 25 x 37 cm) in forced perspective near camera, with the true-size Alice's arm through it; Pat and the CGI White Rabbit placed deep in the yard

scale_notes.rule: The same brick bonds, window divisions and slate colour on the 1:1 and 1:3 builds so the cut is invisible.

negative: no thatch, no half-timbered Tudor cottage, no storybook crooked walls
no rabbit-shaped or carrot decoration, no cartoon motifs
no stone Cotswold cottage; this is brick
no gamekeeper's cottage or estate lodge styling
no plate-glass windows, no porch conservatory, no gas or electric lamps outside
no fittings or props later than 1862 apart from the licensed Art Nouveau ornament (WR-010); no Gothic pointed arches
no cartoon rabbit, no human in rabbit costume; no flat poster illustration or matte-painting finish
prompt_ready_en: a neat little two-storey red brick cottage with pale yellow brick bands and horseshoe-curved window heads under carved lily-and-vine hood moulds, Art Nouveau details in the style of Mucha, a round stained-glass roundel in the gable and a pastel-and-gold mosaic vine frieze under the eaves, steep blue-grey slate roof with a few loose slates, a broad brick chimney stack at the gable with clay pots, a bottle-green front door with a bright brass plate engraved W. RABBIT in a whiplash border, white sash windows, and at the back a kitchen-garden yard with a wooden cucumber-frame under the upstairs window and an old apple tree, at the edge of a wood, photographed live-action set
